head: 87b09093158f487ce277c975f036f7a962ee45cf
classification_reasons: Spec stays tight through the build: Flagged concerns is still 'none', the one open question from intent.md is answered in spec.md's Design with a stated rationale, and Acceptance is measurable (the exact string 'whole must not be zero', two named pre-existing tests still passing, pytest count 10, compileall and ruff healthy output) — the diff delivers exactly that string and exactly that shape.

Blast radius is small and below every routine threshold: the diff touches only sample_pkg/calc.py (the percent function body), tests/test_calc.py (one new test function) and this change's own plan/spec/status/evidence files; no .claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md or sdlc.yaml in the diff; no sdlc.yaml risk_list item (auth, data migrations, money movement, production config) applies to an in-process arithmetic helper; no schema, migration, config or public-signature change (percent's signature and return type are unchanged).

The changed branch is already covered by a pre-existing test: test_percent_zero_whole_raises (present on HEAD before this change) already calls percent(1, 0) and asserts pytest.raises(ZeroDivisionError) over the exact branch the fix touches; the new test only tightens the existing assertion to the literal message, it does not open a new code path.
attempted: Intent: compared intent.md's Proposed outcome (message names 'whole', exception type ZeroDivisionError unchanged, divide's own message unchanged, a test written first and failing before the fix, three green targets) against the actual diff. sample_pkg/calc.py now wraps divide(part * 100, whole) in try/except ZeroDivisionError and re-raises ZeroDivisionError('whole must not be zero') from None, exactly as designed; divide() is byte-for-byte untouched; the new test asserts the exact message. Nothing solves a nearby problem instead of this one.

Spec and plan: plan.md's 'Files that change' lists tests/test_calc.py then sample_pkg/calc.py; the actual commit sequence on this branch (f1f5fc5 'reproducing test' touching only tests/test_calc.py, then 82549de 'catch zero whole...' touching only sample_pkg/calc.py, then 87b0909 'verifier evidence') follows that same order and plan.md's own Order of work (write/fail the test, implement, verify). The Design's catch-and-reraise-with-from-None shape is implemented literally, including 'from None', which plan.md's Risks flagged as the one easy way to depart from spec silently. No part of spec.md or plan.md is left unaddressed; Flagged concerns in spec.md is 'none', so there was nothing to close.

Proof: no test.log/build.log/lint.log exist yet for this phase's own commit (expected: SDLC_GATE_COMMANDS=runner means this CI session defers the gate's own commands check to the runner, and verifier.md says so plainly rather than claiming a run it didn't do — 'read, not run', the case the brief treats as not a proof gap). What verifier.md does offer is a direct interpreter exercise of the changed behavior (percent(1,0) raising with the new message and __cause__ is None; divide(5,0) unchanged; percent(25,50) still correct), plus a read of the actual diff against plan.md/spec.md, and that is literal, not a bare claim. evidence/failing-test.log is literal pytest output showing the new test failing against the pre-fix code with the exact 'b must not be zero' vs 'whole must not be zero' diff pytest reports, so the test is not vacuous.

Blast radius: read the diff's file list directly (sample_pkg/calc.py, tests/test_calc.py, plus this change's own plan.md/spec.md/status.yaml/evidence/*) and sdlc.yaml's risk_list and protected_paths; nothing outside changes/0015-*/** and the two source files is touched, no guardrail file appears in the diff, no risk-list item applies.

Policies: read coding-standards and definition-of-done skills directly. Rule 2 (match the existing error-handling idiom) is followed — catch-and-reraise instead of a duplicate pre-check, as spec.md's Open questions section argues. Rule 4 (a behavior change ships with a failing-first test) is satisfied and evidenced in failing-test.log. Rule 5/8 (no new dependency, lint clean) hold — the diff adds no import and no dependency. CLAUDE.md's 'Things Claude gets wrong' Layout-staleness rule does not apply: no public function was added or removed, and plan.md explicitly says so rather than staying silent.

Tests: test_percent_zero_whole_raises and test_divide_by_zero_raises are present in tests/test_calc.py byte-for-byte unmodified (compared against the diff hunk, which only inserts a new function after the existing ones) — a fix-type change must not touch pre-existing tests, and it doesn't. The new test could not pass against the old code (failing-test.log proves this) and cannot pass with the bug still present, since it asserts the literal new string rather than just the exception type.
Skip markers: grepped the diff for skip/xfail/pytest.ini exclusions — none added. plan.md declares none needed and none appears.

Not used as a reason: no deterministic gate/skill check was re-run or cited as a reason; the reasons above come from reading intent.md, spec.md, plan.md, sdlc.yaml, REVIEW.md, the coding-standards/definition-of-done skills, calc.py, test_calc.py and the committed evidence files directly. The hook-log.jsonl entries showing compileall/pytest/ruff invoked mid-session are the writer's own self-check before committing (plan.md step 3), not the gate's deferred commands-check record, and are consistent with the deferred-to-runner model rather than contradicting it.
